title: Diesel engine basics for future diagnostic expansion
whatItIs: Diesel engines control torque mainly by fuel quantity and air management rather than a stoichiometric throttle strategy. Boost, rail pressure, EGR and aftertreatment dominate many diesel faults.
normalValues: Normal diesel values vary strongly by engine and enhanced PIDs. Generic OBD-II gives only a partial picture, so the app treats diesel conclusions more conservatively unless profile and PIDs are rich.
deviations: Low boost with smoke or low torque suggests air management
Rail pressure tracking error suggests fuel supply or high-pressure system
EGR/DPF faults can change airflow and backpressure
Glow and compression issues dominate cold start
influence: This app's current root-cause benchmark is gasoline-focused, but the architecture keeps diesel knowledge separate so future diesel support can be added without corrupting gasoline rules.
checks: Use diesel-specific enhanced PIDs when available
Compare requested and actual rail pressure/boost/EGR
Check DPF differential pressure and regeneration state
Do not apply gasoline fuel-trim logic to diesel
